```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(metamicrobiomeR)
```

Version 2.0 is a redesign and does **not** read the 1.x input format or provide the 1.x
functions. Version 1.3 (branch `legacy-1.x` on GitHub) is the last release with the old interface.

## Function map

| 1.x | 2.0 |
|---|---|
| `read.multi()`, QIIME 1 tables | `as_study()`, `read_dada2()`, `read_qiime2()`, `read_metaphlan()`, `read_biom_study()`, `study_from_phyloseq()`, `study_from_se()` |
| `taxa.filter()` | filters inside `fit_study()` (`min_prevalence`, `min_mean`) |
| `taxa.compare(propmed.rel = "gamlss")` | `fit_study(engine = "bezi_gamlss", n_cycles = 20)` reproduces it |
| `taxa.compare(propmed.rel = "lm", transform = "asin.sqrt")` | `fit_study(engine = "lm_asin")` |
| `pathway.compare()` | `read_function_table()` then `fit_study()` |
| `alpha.compare()` | `fit_alpha()` |
| `meta.taxa()` | `pool_effects(method = "DL", test = "z", adjust_by = c("part", "term"))` reproduces it |
| `metatab.show()`, `meta.niceplot()` | `plot_forest()` |
| `microbiomeage()`, `taxa.mean.plot()`, `taxa.meansdn()`, `taxcomtab.show()` | removed |

## Defaults that changed, and why

* **GAMLSS iterations:** 100 instead of 20. At 20, most fits on real data did not converge.
* **Unassigned lineages** (`...f__lachnospiraceae.other`) are excluded from models.
* **Pooling:** REML with the ad hoc Hartung-Knapp test instead of DerSimonian-Laird with a
  normal test; features need estimates from at least two studies (1.x could "pool" a single study).
* **False discovery rate** is adjusted within a rank, not across all ranks mixed.
* **1.x errors fixed in 1.3 and not carried over:** mixed-model p-values were 2% too small,
  adjusted p-value column names were truncated at the last dot, and the GMPR transform
  returned only missing values.

## Converting an old wide table

A 1.x table has samples in rows, sample variables and taxa in columns, and QIIME 1 style names.
This converts such a table to a study object (the same steps were used to validate 2.0
against the 2019 results; the name parsing handles the `.other` padding of unassigned levels):

```{r convert}
old <- data.frame(
  sample = paste0("S", 1:4), group = c("a", "b", "a", "b"),
  `k__bacteria.p__firmicutes` = c(0.6, 0.5, 0.7, 0.4),
  `k__bacteria.p__bacteroidetes` = c(0.4, 0.5, 0.3, 0.6),
  `k__bacteria.p__firmicutes.c__clostridia` = c(0.5, 0.4, 0.6, 0.3),
  `k__bacteria.p__firmicutes.c__clostridia.other` = c(0.1, 0.1, 0.1, 0.1),
  check.names = FALSE)
taxa_cols <- grep("^k__", colnames(old), value = TRUE)

# 1. the level of a column: number of rank tokens plus ".other" padding
extra <- lengths(regmatches(taxa_cols, gregexpr("\\.other", taxa_cols)))
clean <- gsub("\\.other", "", taxa_cols)
ntok  <- lengths(regmatches(clean, gregexpr("\\.(?=[a-z]__)", clean, perl = TRUE))) + 1
level <- c("kingdom", "phylum", "class", "order", "family", "genus", "species")[ntok + extra]

# 2. taxonomy in rank columns
tax <- parse_taxonomy(gsub("\\.(?=[a-z]__)", ";", clean, perl = TRUE))
rownames(tax) <- taxa_cols
tax <- tax[, colSums(!is.na(tax)) > 0 & colnames(tax) != "deepest", drop = FALSE]
tax$rank <- level

# 3. features by samples
rel <- t(as.matrix(old[, taxa_cols])); colnames(rel) <- old$sample
study <- as_study(relabund = rel, taxonomy = tax, samples = data.frame(group = old$group, row.names = old$sample),
                  study = list(id = "old_study", feature_type = "otu", database = "Greengenes 13.8"))
study
mm_features(study)[, c("phylum", "class", "rank")]
```

Note that old tables hold relative abundances only: the count-based engine
(`"zibb_glmmtmb"`) needs counts, so it cannot be used on them. The 1.x sample data of studies
obtained from investigators are not distributed with the package.
